title: Development Environment & Tooling
description: Set up a safe repeatable workspace and understand files, terminals, editors, runtimes, dependencies, and build tools.

lessons.title: The project directory
lessons.principle: A working directory contains source, configuration, tests, documentation, and generated output with different roles.
lessons.practice: Identify the repository root and distinguish committed files from generated or local files.

lessons.title: Inspect before editing
lessons.principle: A file tree conveys architecture clues but not every file is safe to modify or commit.
lessons.practice: Read README and local contributor instructions, then ask AI to summarize the files relevant to the task.

lessons.title: Terminal basics
lessons.principle: Commands execute programs within a current directory and environment, often with filesystem side effects.
lessons.practice: Practice pwd, ls or dir, cd, mkdir, and reading text files on a disposable project.

lessons.title: Avoid destructive copy-paste
lessons.principle: Shell commands from model outputs may delete files, leak data, or execute downloaded content.
lessons.practice: Explain each unfamiliar flag before running commands; do not pipe unknown remote scripts into a shell.

lessons.title: Editors and diagnostics
lessons.principle: A code editor exposes syntax errors, references, formatting, version history, and breakpoints.
lessons.practice: Use project-wide search and navigate to the definitions of changed symbols.

lessons.title: Use diagnostics as evidence
lessons.principle: Squiggles and type errors identify potential issues but do not cover all runtime behavior.
lessons.practice: Copy exact diagnostic text into an AI request and verify its proposed fix in the editor.

lessons.title: Language and runtime
lessons.principle: Source language, interpreter or runtime version, and operating system determine what executes.
lessons.practice: Record required Node or Python version and the project entry point.

lessons.title: Match local and target environments
lessons.principle: A feature that works locally may fail under a different runtime or configuration.
lessons.practice: Pin or document supported runtime versions and test the one used for release.

lessons.title: Packages and dependency manifests
lessons.principle: Package manifests declare direct dependencies, scripts, and metadata, while lockfiles resolve exact versions.
lessons.practice: Explain the difference between a manifest and a generated lockfile.

lessons.title: Install reproducibly
lessons.principle: Non-repeatable installs can produce different behavior on teammates' computers or CI.
lessons.practice: Use the project's lockfile-aware installation command and review proposed new dependencies.

lessons.title: Environment variables and secrets
lessons.principle: Configuration differs across environments; credentials must not become source-controlled data or browser bundles.
lessons.practice: Use documented sample variable names with placeholder values.

lessons.title: Handle local secrets safely
lessons.principle: A .env file is not automatically protected if it is committed, logged, or included in a build.
lessons.practice: Ignore secret-bearing files, use secret stores in deployment, and rotate any accidentally exposed credential.

lessons.title: Local servers and ports
lessons.principle: A development server binds to a host and port and can differ from a production web server.
lessons.practice: Launch a minimal project and verify the actual listening URL.

lessons.title: Distinguish exposure levels
lessons.principle: Listening only on localhost is not equivalent to exposing a service on all network interfaces.
lessons.practice: Check bind address, firewall, authentication, and whether the test server contains real data.

lessons.title: Build, lint, and type checking
lessons.principle: Build tools transform assets, linters flag patterns, and type checkers validate declared type relationships.
lessons.practice: Find the project's actual scripts instead of inventing standard names.

lessons.title: Understand check limitations
lessons.principle: A green build does not prove security, accessibility, or correct feature behavior.
lessons.practice: Run the most relevant syntax, type, test, and browser checks and report each separately.

lessons.title: Containers at a beginner level
lessons.principle: A container packages an application process with a defined filesystem and environment, but it is not a security boundary by itself.
lessons.practice: Explain image, container, Dockerfile, volume, and port mapping in one example.

lessons.title: Keep mutable data separate
lessons.principle: Container filesystems can be replaced and should not be the only home of persistent business data.
lessons.practice: Use named volumes or external storage where appropriate and avoid baking secrets into images.

lessons.title: Reproducible onboarding
lessons.principle: A reliable project can be cloned, configured, started, checked, and stopped by someone new.
lessons.practice: Write a short setup guide with prerequisites and expected results.

lessons.title: Test the setup from scratch
lessons.principle: An undocumented global package or local file can hide a broken onboarding flow.
lessons.practice: Ask a fresh clone or isolated environment to follow README commands and record any missing steps.

codeExamples.snippet:
# Run only after reviewing the repository instructions
pwd
ls -la
node --version
npm --version
npm run

FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
COPY . .
USER node
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
